In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

AG-1 recognizes an as yet undefined low-mol-wr glycoprotein on the human platelet membrane that may be involved as a mediator of platelet activation and aggregation, and that may interact with subpopulations of the glycoprotein Ib complex.
AG-1 recognizes a platelet membrane glycoprotein of mol wt 20,000-28,000 dalton that may function as a receptor for platelet activation.
AG-1 binds to a platelet surface protein of mol wt approximately 21, 000 that appears distinct from the major glycoproteins and may be involved in platelet aggregation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have produced a monoclonal antibody that recognizes a low-mol-wl glycoprotein of the human platelet membrane that is involved in platelet aggregation and that may be involved with the platelet glycoprotein Ib complex.

AG-1 recognizes a platelet membrane surface glycoprotein that appears to be distinct from the major platelet membrane glycoproteins, but which may function in concert with glycoproteins Ib, IX, and IIb/III in platelet activation and aggregation.

AG-1 recognizes a platelet membrane glycoprotein of mol wt approximately 21,500 that may be associated with platelet aggregation and that may interact with the beta-chain of glycoprotein IIb and the beta-chains and/or the heavy chains of glycoprotein IX and/or glycoprotein Ib.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a low-mol-wl protein, distinct from known platelet membrane proteins, may be involved in platelet aggregation.
the low-mol wt protein recognized by AG- 1 may be involved in platelet activation and may represent an important component of the platelet membrane involved in platelet aggregation.
